features: Plain-English intake — `exec-agent do "..."` resolves the repo and infers a check, or hands off to the planner
Multi-task decomposition — one brain call breaks an objective into a dependency-ordered task graph
Per-objective failure policy — escalate | abandon | skip when a task exhausts its attempts
Persistent supervisor daemon — closing the terminal, or the laptop, does not stop the work
git worktree isolation — a dedicated branch per attempt, nothing runs against your working tree
Policy engine — denies or asks about force-push, prod deploys, destructive SQL, committed secrets
Verification gate — the supervisor runs your real acceptance command; a worker's own "done" is advisory
Independent judge — reviews each attempt's diff against intent before it counts as done, so a worker's own "done" is never the final word
Cause-aware recovery — a failure diagnoser classifies flaky, bug, spec, or environment, and picks retry, retry-with-hint, respawn, or escalate
Checkpoint & respawn — a fresh worker is seeded with what was tried and ruled out, not a longer chat
Rate-limit park-and-resume — retried in place once the limit clears, never burns the attempt budget
Standing engineering profile — preferences that shape every planning, review, and diagnosis call
Decisions answerable anywhere — terminal, `exec-agent decide`, the dashboard, or the iOS app
Human approval gate — a diff per branch and a Merge button; nothing is ever merged automatically
Full event log per objective — `exec-agent events <id>`, replayable, the actual source of truth
Daemon autostart on login/reboot — with visibility in the dashboard
Dashboard attribution — which model did the work, what the judge and diagnoser decided, and who answered an escalation and through which channel
Local knowledge-graph tool — graphify builds a per-repo call graph with zero LLM tokens; the worker, judge, and diagnoser query it via MCP instead of re-grepping raw files on every attempt
Dashboard knowledge-graph panel — node/edge/community counts, an extracted/inferred/ambiguous confidence breakdown, and the most-connected code per objective
iOS companion app (in development) — follow every objective live from your iPhone: tasks, attempts, cost, activity, and the decisions waiting on you
Answer from your phone — each option with its pros, cons and risk, the agent's recommendation pre-selected, applied by your computer the instant you confirm
Agent file tree — browse every file each agent added, modified, deleted or renamed, without the code ever leaving your computer

Private cloud relay — the daemon syncs status, costs, decisions and file names out over outbound connections only; source code and diffs stay on your machine, and every table is locked to you by row-level security

Merge from your phone — review what changed, the judge's verdict, and which repo it lands in, then Merge & Push; the same lock-guarded path as the dashboard, and it stops safely on uncommitted changes
Push notifications (in development) — your phone buzzes when a decision needs you, work is ready to merge, or an objective fails; titles only, never code
Honest reviews — a judge that fails is retried, and if it still can't give a verdict the work is marked "not reviewed", never silently accepted
Insights — spend over the last 30 days, spend by model, and the week's health, on your phone
Say what you want from your phone (in development) — a chat with history, like the Claude app: pick a repo, describe the work, and follow it as a conversation, from plan to merge
Understands what isn't work — "thanks" gets a reply, not a run; a request it can't do gets an honest answer; finished work that changed nothing never offers a merge

entries: Released `v3.0.0` — Praktor now goes with you: start work, answer its questions, and merge the result from your iPhone, while the work itself never leaves your computer
Added a Claude-style chat to the app — say what you want in your own words, pick the repo, and follow it as a conversation; follow-ups carry what came before
Messages that aren't work no longer start any — "thanks" gets a reply for free, an impossible request gets an honest answer, and work that changed nothing never offers a merge

Merge finished work from your iPhone — see what changed, the judge's verdict, and the target repo, then Merge & Push through the same lock-guarded path as the dashboard; a dirty repo or a conflict stops it safely and tells you why
Added push notifications — when a decision needs you, work is ready to merge, or an objective fails, each sent once and opening exactly that screen (needs the app's development build)
Fixed a failed review being recorded as accepted — the judge now retries, and work it still can't review is marked "not reviewed" before anyone merges it
The app now says why a computer isn't acting on a request — offline, running an older Praktor that needs a restart, or just slow — instead of spinning
Kept each task's file tree after its branch is merged and cleaned up
Added Insights to the app — 30-day spend by day and by model, and the week's health

Answer an agent's decision from your iPhone — every option with its pros, cons and risk, the recommendation pre-selected, and an explicit confirm; your computer applies it the instant it arrives, through the same path as the terminal, dashboard and Telegram
Fixed "ask me" getting lost between the planner and the worker — every worker now sees your original words, so an instruction to check with you can't be planned away
Fixed the cloud bridge's retry backoff, which reset on every attempt instead of backing off
Started the Praktor iOS app — sign in with Google, pair a computer by scanning a one-time code, and follow every objective live: tasks, attempts, cost, activity, and the file tree each agent built

Added a private cloud relay the daemon syncs to over outbound connections only — status, costs, decisions and file names, never your source code — with every table locked down by row-level security tested against real Postgres
Added `exec-agent cloud connect` — pairs this computer with the app through a single-use, ten-minute code, and refuses to ever store a secret key
Hardened the local dashboard against cross-site requests and DNS rebinding — it now only ever answers this machine
